new.title: Do time in the Gevangenpoort
new.desc: This 15th-century gatehouse once guarded the castle of the Counts of Holland and then served as a jail for four centuries. Cells, interrogation rooms and grim instruments are still inside.
new.tip: Visits are guided; English tours run mainly at weekends, so check the schedule before you go.

new.title: Get lost in Escher's impossible worlds
new.desc: Escher in Het Paleis fills a former royal winter palace on Lange Voorhout with M.C. Escher's endless staircases and tessellations. Upstairs, hands-on optical illusions let you step into the tricks yourself.
new.tip: Look up in every room: the chandeliers were designed especially for the museum and are part of the show.
new.q: Escher in Het Paleis Den Haag

new.title: Say 'hoi' to Haagse Harry
new.desc: The foul-mouthed comic hero of cartoonist Marnix Rueb got his own bronze statue on the Grote Markt in 2016. Over two metres tall, he is the city's unofficial mascot and speaks pure plat Haags.
new.tip: He stands above the tram tunnel entrance with the Grote Kerk tower behind him, the classic photo angle.
new.q: Standbeeld Haagse Harry Grote Markt Den Haag

new.title: Walk under the dragons of Chinatown
new.desc: Two ornate Chinese gates with carved dragon pillars mark the entrances to Den Haag's Chinatown around the Wagenstraat and Sint Jacobsstraat. Behind them: Asian supermarkets, bubble tea and some of the best dim sum in the country.
new.tip: Come during Chinese New Year, when the streets fill with lion dances and firecrackers.

new.title: Find the church hidden behind a front door
new.desc: When Catholic mass was banned, believers worshipped in secret. Behind an ordinary door in the Hofkwartier hides the Oud-Katholieke Kerk, a baroque church you would never guess was there from the street.
new.tip: It looks like a normal house from outside; watch the house numbers on Juffrouw Idastraat.
new.q: Oud-Katholieke Kerk Juffrouw Idastraat 7 Den Haag

new.title: Sneak into the artists' house on Lange Voorhout
new.desc: Pulchri Studio has been the home of a painters' society since the days of Mesdag. Its exhibitions are open to all, and behind the building lies a quiet garden that few passers-by know about.
new.tip: In summer the garden is a lovely spot for a drink, far from the bustle of the city.
new.q: Pulchri Studio Lange Voorhout 15 Den Haag

new.title: Stand on the dune of Panorama Mesdag
new.desc: Climb a fake dune and you are surrounded by a 120-metre painting of Scheveningen in 1881, made by H.W. Mesdag with his wife Sientje and the young Breitner. It is the oldest panorama still in its original building.
new.tip: Give your eyes a minute: the real sand in the foreground and the skylight make the horizon seem endless.

new.title: Lie back in James Turrell's sky crater
new.desc: Hidden in the dunes of Kijkduin, Celestial Vault (Hemels Gewelf) is a grassy elliptical crater with a stone bench at its centre. Lie down and the sky turns into a dome above you.
new.tip: Bring a blanket and go at sunset or on a starry night; a second bench on the dune top looks out over the sea.
new.q: Hemels Gewelf Machiel Vrijenhoeklaan Den Haag

new.title: Visit the oldest building in Den Haag
new.desc: Loosduinen's Abdijkerk was built around 1240 at the request of the wife of Count Floris IV, long before Den Haag was a city. It is all that is left of a monastery destroyed in 1573.
new.tip: The church is open for visitors on Sundays in July and August, often with organ playing. Tram 2 or 3 to the end stop, then a short walk.

new.title: Watch the sails of De Korenaer turn
new.desc: This restored 18th-century corn mill in Loosduinen still grinds grain, run by volunteer millers. The granary at its foot houses a small museum about Loosduinen's market-gardening past.
new.tip: Buy flour or muesli in the mill shop; it was milled a few metres from where you stand.
new.q: Molen De Korenaer Margaretha van Hennebergweg Den Haag

new.title: Wander the fishermen's lanes of Oud Scheveningen
new.desc: Just behind the boulevard, the Keizerstraat leads into the old fishing village with small brick houses and narrow alleys. It feels a world away from the beach crowds a few streets on.
new.tip: Start at the statue of the Scheveningen fisherman's wife and walk down the Keizerstraat towards the harbour.

new.title: Learn the fishing story at Muzee
new.desc: Muzee Scheveningen, in an old school building, tells how the village lived from and with the sea: ship models, period rooms and a sea room with aquariums, shells and fossils.
new.tip: Visit before you eat at the harbour; you'll look at your herring differently.

new.title: Smell the roses in Westbroekpark
new.desc: The international Rosarium in Westbroekpark holds about 20,000 roses on some 300 beds. Every summer a jury judges new varieties in an international rose competition.
new.tip: The beds peak from late June into the summer; visitors can vote for their own favourites too.

new.title: Find James Bond's Aston Martin at the Louwman
new.desc: The Louwman Museum holds one of the oldest private car collections in the world, from an 1887 De Dion Bouton to Elvis's Cadillac and the DB5 from Goldfinger. A hidden wing even holds a large collection of historic telescopes.
new.tip: It sits at the edge of the Haagse Bos, so combine it with a walk or bike ride through the forest.

new.title: Sip a Haagse liqueur at Van Kleef
new.desc: Founded in 1842, Van Kleef is the last genever and liqueur distillery left in a city that once had dozens. Old copper stills and walls of 'drankorgels' still stand in the shop.
new.tip: Ask to taste the Haagse liqueurs with local names, like Bruidstranen or Haags Hopje.
new.q: Museum Van Kleef Lange Beestenmarkt 109 Den Haag

new.title: Grab a kroket at Dungelmann
new.desc: This butcher's on the Hoogstraat is famous for one thing: the Dungelmann croquette, often named the best in town. Locals eat it standing outside on a slice of white bread.
new.tip: Add mustard and eat it right away while the inside is still molten.

new.title: Share dim sum at Full Moon City
new.desc: Up an escalator in Chinatown, this huge Cantonese restaurant seats over 230 people and its dim sum is made fresh every day by chefs from Hong Kong and Guangdong.
new.tip: Book ahead at weekends and come with a group so you can order lots of little baskets.
new.q: Full Moon City Achter Raamstraat 75 Den Haag

new.title: Breakfast in the secret garden of Het Nutshuis
new.desc: Café Soof sits in a courtyard garden behind Het Nutshuis, among fruit and nut trees, beehives and a lily pond. A green escape right in the shopping centre.
new.tip: Go on a sunny morning; the garden fills up fast at lunchtime.

new.title: Order a rijsttafel at Toko Frederik
new.desc: Den Haag has more toko's than any other Dutch city, a legacy of the many Indo families who settled here after 1945. Toko Frederik has been a local favourite for over thirty years.
new.tip: Its rijsttafel is the house speciality; the Frederikstraat itself is worth a browse afterwards.

new.title: Eat East Javanese at Keraton Damai
new.desc: Near the Peace Palace, this Indonesian restaurant cooks East Javanese dishes the way the owners' mothers made them. Warm service, home-style flavours.
new.tip: Combine it with an evening walk past the Peace Palace once the lights come on.
new.q: Keraton Damai Groot Hertoginnelaan 57 Den Haag

new.title: Have roti at Tropisch Huis Addoel
new.desc: For more than four decades this family place near the Haagse Markt has been serving Surinamese food to the neighbourhood. It is a taste of the Schilderswijk and Transvaal at their most authentic.
new.tip: Pair it with a morning at the Haagse Markt, a few minutes' walk away.
new.q: Tropisch Huis Addoel Paul Krugerplein 22 Den Haag

new.title: Pull yourself across to De Waterkant
new.desc: This little tearoom hidden in Westbroekpark is reached by a hand-pulled ferry from the Haringkade. Scones, high tea and rowing boats for hire make it a summer favourite.
new.tip: It only opens in the warm season, roughly from King's Day to Prinsjesdag.
new.q: Theesalon De Waterkant Westbroekpark Den Haag

new.title: Coffee at 't Puntje, the end of the beach
new.desc: At the very northern tip of Scheveningen's beach, where the dunes take over, sits the cosy beach café 't Puntje. Quieter than the boulevard and with a view of nothing but sand and sea.
new.tip: Walk or cycle there along the dunes from the Pier; it makes a perfect halfway stop.

new.title: Taste a Haagse Kakker at Hessing
new.desc: Bakkerij Hessing in Bezuidenhout specialises in Haagse treats: the Haagse Kakker, Ooievaartjes and a Haagsche Hopjes cake, plus a range of sourdough bread.
new.tip: The original Haagsche Hopjes sweets are no longer made, so the Hopjes cake here is one of the few ways left to taste that coffee-caramel flavour.

new.title: Drink a Kompaan at the brewery
new.desc: Den Haag's best-known craft brewery has its home base in an industrial hall on the Binckhorst harbour. Its barrel-aged specials are sold in small batches straight from the brewery.
new.tip: Book a tasting to hear the story of the brewery; the bar is only open a few days a week.

new.title: Picnic in the King's garden
new.desc: The Paleistuin behind Paleis Noordeinde is a royal garden open to everyone, with lawns, old trees and a small playground right in the city centre.
new.tip: Enter by the Prinsessewal or via the Koningspoort on the Molenstraat, a little royal shortcut from the shops.

new.title: Climb the tower of the Grote Kerk
new.desc: The hexagonal 15th-century tower of the Grote Kerk is one of the tallest church towers in the country. Hundreds of steps take you up past the carillon to a view over the whole city and the sea.
new.tip: The tower opens only on certain days, so check the church's website before you go.

new.title: Hear a Bach cantata in the Kloosterkerk
new.desc: The 15th-century Kloosterkerk on Lange Voorhout hosts a monthly Bach cantata performance. Physicist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit lies buried here.
new.tip: Keep an eye on its agenda for second-hand bazaars too.

new.title: Ride a vintage tram from the HOVM
new.desc: The Haags Openbaar Vervoer Museum fills an old 1906 tram depot with historic trams and buses. On Sundays you can combine a visit with a ride on a vintage tram through the city.
new.tip: It is only open on Sunday afternoons; in December there are special winter rides.
new.q: Haags Openbaar Vervoer Museum Parallelweg 224 Den Haag

new.title: Climb De Vulkaan and spot Highland cattle
new.desc: Westduinpark is a wild dune park between Kijkduin and Scheveningen, grazed by shaggy Scottish Highlanders. Its highest point, De Vulkaan, is a favourite local lookout over dunes and city.
new.tip: Keep your distance from the cattle and keep dogs on a lead near them.

new.title: Ride the Ferris wheel on De Pier
new.desc: The pier stretches out into the North Sea from Scheveningen beach, with a Ferris wheel at its head. From the top you see the whole coastline and the city skyline.
new.tip: Go around sunset, when the light over the sea is at its best, and walk back along the boulevard afterwards.

new.title: Welcome Sinterklaas in the harbour
new.desc: Every November Sinterklaas sails into Scheveningen harbour on his steamboat and then parades into the city. Thousands of children wait on the quays.
new.tip: Get there early for a spot along the quay; trams to the harbour are packed.
new.q: Scheveningen Haven Dr. Lelykade Den Haag

new.title: Walk out on the Zuiderhavenhoofd
new.desc: The southern harbour pier on the Duindorp side is a walk straight into the sea with views of the ships coming in. Birdwatchers come for turnstones, purple sandpipers and, in winter, snow buntings.
new.tip: Wrap up warm and bring binoculars; the pier is only accessible on foot, so park near the Zuiderstrandtheater.

new.title: Get lost in the Scheveningse Bosjes
new.desc: This dune forest between the city and the sea is full of winding paths, ponds and playgrounds. It is where Hagenaars walk the dog and cycle to the beach.
new.tip: Bike through it on your way to Scheveningen instead of taking the main road.

new.title: Hunt street art in the Binckhorst
new.desc: The old industrial Binckhorst is turning into a creative quarter, and its warehouse walls are covered with murals. Former factories now house a club, a skatepark and studios.
new.tip: Start at the corner of Melkwegstraat and Saturnusstraat and end with a beer at Kompaan; The Hague Street Art has an online map.
